newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Ship carrying relief to Albania unloads in Durres.
newsitem.headline: Ship carrying relief to Albania unloads in Durres.

text.p: A ship carrying about 400 tonnes of humanitarian aid supplies from the U.N.'s World Food Programme (WFP) began unloading in the western Albanian port of Durres on Wednesday.

It is the biggest food shipment to Albania since the launch of a multinational aid protection mission to the chaotic Balkan state. A WFP worker in Durres said the supplies would be stored in a port warehouse until deliveries could begin on Friday.

"We are planning to make our first distribution on Friday," said Sasha Zarkovacki, a WFP official. The WFP was discussing a strategy to distribute the aid in cooperation with the Italian-led multinational force that landed on Tuesday.

Albania slid into anarchy last month after fraudulent investment schemes wiped out the saving of thousands of families. Nearly 300 people have been killed since people looted armouries deserted by soldiers and police.
The Greek-owned ship Stavros Emmanuel, carrying 360 tonnes of wheat flour and 36 tonnes of beans, began unloading supplies on Wednesday morning in Durres, 40 km (25 miles) west of Tirana.

The head of the WFP Albania mission, Jean-Marie Boucher, said on Tuesday the relief programme would last for several months and was destined for hospitals, orphanages, homes for the handicapped and elderly and destitute families in Albania.
"As this is not a famine, we are acting as a bridge until things return to normal," Boucher said.
Albania's poor desperately need food. Basic food costs have shot up, social security payments have stopped and state food supplies are not reaching institutions, aid officials said.

Relief agencies estimate that one in 10 Albanians needs humanitarian aid. The Geneva-based International Committee of the Red Cross, which does not rely on armed escorts, has been distributing food and medicines since last month.

Nearly 1,200 Italian, French and Spanish soldiers belonging to the eight-nation U.N.-backed force arrived by land and sea in Albania on Tuesday at the start of a mission to protect delivery of emergency food aid and medicines to the country's poor.
On Friday, the WFP hopes to transport 101 tonnes of wheat flour to destitute families in Elbasan, a central Albanian town 50 km (30 miles) southeast of Tirana.
Another convoy of trucks is planning to transport 200 tonnes of relief supplies to Kukes, a remote mountain town 208 km (125 miles) northeast of Tirana.
The WFP said it considers those areas to be relatively safe. It has nevertheless requested armed escorts to protect the convoys.
Aside from that, private vans from other parts of Albania are planning to pick up smaller amounts of the supplies and ferry them back to their institutions without escorts.
The Stavros Emmanuel arrived in Durres on Tuesday after sailing from the Italian port of Trieste.
Another ship carrying 23 tonnes of vegetable oil was due to arrive from the southeastern Italian port of Brindisi within the next day or two, the WFP said.
